description: Turns an existing invoice PDF into an EN 16931 e-invoice (ZUGFeRD / Factur-X) without changing how it looks. TypeScript library, CLI, MCP server and browser app; runs locally.
rules: Act for the invoice issuer only: a recipient cannot turn a received PDF into a valid e-invoice.
Copy values exactly as the PDF prints them and never invent a missing one; ask the user instead.

Call check(draft, { pdfText }) before createEInvoice and show the findings: errors block the file, warnings need a second look. createEInvoice throws an InvoiceError with the findings while errors are open.
Read the text with extractLayout(pdf) and get a first draft with guessFromText(text, { blocks }); it is a starting point, not a result.
Data read by a language model goes through keepWhatThePdfShows(draft, text) before it is used.
The XML is the binding part of the e-invoice and must not contradict the visible PDF; the user confirms the data before the file is created.
Every VAT category except S has vatRate 0; all of those except Z need vatExemptionReason. AE and K need buyer.vatId.
Document-level discounts are not modelled: enter them as a line with a negative quantity.
Node 22.13 or newer. In a browser the bundler needs an alias from @e-invoice-eu/core to its browser bundle and the pdf.js worker; see site/vite.config.ts and site/main.ts.
validateEInvoice is a plausibility check, not a full EN 16931 validation.
